posts.author: Nolgoth
posts.body:
Hello all, I am in need of some help and I hope someone here might be able to. I am in a game design class for college as part of my computer science (AS) degree. We are in teams of 4 and was tasked with making our own games with whatever engines we want, I chose RPGMaker MV as I already owned it.
The others in the group decided that they want to make a horror game based on a space station. I was thinking of making something that had the sense of a dungeon crawler, start at a safe zone and make your way through say 100 levels (inspiration is the Ancient Cave in Lufia 2) with important events and significant difficulty increases on every 5-10 levels.
I think I can cobble together the programming but here's where I am requesting help: we are going to need assets for anything horror related for enemies, tile sets for the environment, a map of the space station, etc. We do not have any art people on the team to make any of this stuff. I am thinking of something like Event Horizon, the Alien franchise, Dead Space, with The Thing sprinkled in as inspirations. Any assets gleaned from this site will have appropriate credit going to the people that created them in the final project's roll credits screen.
This game is not going to be commercial at all, I am not expecting AAA level work on it either, just trying to create something that fills the requirements of the class (something that works with 10 minutes or more of gameplay for testing with no bugs/glitches). Any further questions feel free to reach out.
Thanks

posts.author: I_LIKE_BREAD7
posts.body:
If you don't need custom resources you might want to look into royalty-free resources.
Here's an entire website dedicated to providing free (both royalty-free and free of charge) game resources.
OpenGameArt.org
opengameart.org
There are also a lot of resources on itch.io, some of them are paid, but there are also a lot of free ones too.
Top game assets
Find game assets like Ansimuz Legacy Collection, Godot VFX & Effects collection, Modern Interiors - RPG Tileset [16X16], Tiny Swords, Universal Animation Library on itch.io, the indie game hosting marketplace
itch.io
You can also check out the resources people have posted on this forum so far in these sections
General Resources
This board is for resources that can be used in all RPG Maker versions. Do not post rips. The resources must be your own or have permission to post!
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
RPG Maker MV Resources
forums.rpgmakerweb.com

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
The more specific your request, the more likely that anyone can point you into the right direction. Similar to I_LIKE_BREAD7, all I could do right now would be to vaguely point into the directions of the sites where one would get resources in general.
Personally, a tip from someone who pulled through with an (university, but similar to) school project twice:
RPG Maker and your education - maybe you can combine it?
I recently graduated with a Master of Science, and while it might sound hilarious at first, I did so by creating a game in RPG Maker MZ. Since it worked really well for me and there is quite a lot of potential there, I wanted to write this essay/tutorial about combining your hobby with your...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Scope is a defining criteria, and scope also matches the assets. Before you clock in with your teacher that that is what you can deliver for sure, either make sure you have the resources or that you are able to get the resource - vaguely relying on a forum of strangers is not securing your assets.
For example: my concepts where built with the knowledge in mind that I could do everything myself (aka I was 100% independent), but that I HAD to then do that (aka that I only had so much time and every time that went to assets was missing elsewhere).
Working entirely with free assets is very possible, but requires you (or whoever manages that in your team) the knowledge to format everything as you need since your settings are less likely to come across in perfect plug and play format and amount of content.
If you have a very clear image in your head, you can get better results by making specific requests, like for the space station, as you can see in the request template:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/resource-request-form.49495/
Just naming references does not work, cause I (and many others) are not going to research how you want your project to look like, you better just make a better description in the first place

Thanks, but that's not what this class is about. It is an introduction to game design. We are not expected to know everything about how to make a game nor how to use the engines we are going to use (though of course prior experience is helpful). We have many various options the professor listed (unity, java, unreal, godot, gamemaker, rpgmaker, etc). Also, project is due in December, so we have time to work on stuff and learn as we go. Also, the professor has no say in what we make or how we make it as long as it has no pornography or overly gratuitous violence (like no games about shooting up schools or extreme Mortal Kombat style games) just her personal preferences.
The goal of each team is to try to have one coder, one art person, one musician, one writer, etc but we can only have teams of 4 and not everyone in the class can even do many of the stuff we need. Like I have a guy (56 year old) on my team that has *never* played a video game in his life.
The specific game idea was agreed upon by the other 3 members of the team, the only say I got was what engine we were going to use (since I already own MV and one team member was familiar with XP) and that the game will be an RPG. I would have been much happier if it was standard fantasy but they are really gung-ho about wanting it to be horror.
I am already making some headway with gathering assets from the free resource sites provided.
